To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of preoperative chemotherapy to primary surgical therapy results in a significant increase in breast-conservation surgery and a reduction in local recurrence in patients with operable breast cancer, without a reduction in disease-free survival or overall survival.

(1) preoperative chemotherapy is associated with an increase in the number of patients who can be treated with conservative surgery, but (2) this increase is not sufficient to justify the use of this therapy for all patients with operable breast cancer.
the addition of preoperative chemotherapy to surgery and radiation therapy in operable breast cancer patients results in a higher rate of breast conservation, but does not improve overall survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the response of breast cancer cells to chemotherapy and to the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of breast cancers that are refractory to standard therapy.
the identification and validation of the molecular mechanisms of action of cytotoxic drugs in human tumors.
the development of new therapeutic modalities, including preoperative chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the treatment of breast carcinoma, primary medical therapy is an important research strategy that is not currently a standard of care.
, at present, there is no clear indication to use preoperative chemotherapy in the management of operable breast carcinoma.
the use of preoperative chemotherapy in operable breast cancer has been shown to be feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of preoperative chemotherapy should be limited to randomized trials.
the preoperative chemotherapy should be reserved for patients in randomized studies.
preoperative chemotherapy should be limited to the treatment of patients with locally advanced disease, in whom it is used to convert the tumor into a more operable state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have to do more research on the role of preoperative chemotherapy in breast cancer.
the current paradigm of preoperative therapy, which was developed to increase breast conservation, is no longer appropriate.
the preoperative use of doxorubicin-based therapy in the management primary breast cancer is associated with an increase in the proportion of patients who undergo breast conservation.
